hero.title: Reproducing Exactly A 500 Word English Text
hero.description: Part-B of the Allahabad High Court RO/ARO examination features a mandatory Computer Knowledge and Typing Test. Candidates must reproduce a given 500-word English text on a computer within 20 minutes, requiring a minimum speed of 25 WPM with high accuracy, where evaluation strictly penalizes formatting and spelling errors.

timeline.title: Evolution of Typing Standards and Examination Formats
timeline.description: Chronological milestones in keyboard layouts, typing speed metrics, and Allahabad High Court recruitment exam patterns.

cards.details: The Sholes and Glidden typewriter introduced the QWERTY layout, which became the global standard for mechanical and electronic text reproduction.
Establishment of Words Per Minute (WPM) calculated as (Total Characters / 5) / Time, standardizing professional typing assessment globally.
Allahabad High Court transitioned the RO/ARO typing test from traditional typewriters/offline systems to computer-based software evaluation.
National Testing Agency (NTA) standardized the single-day CBT exam followed immediately by the 500-word exact reproduction typing test.

items.question: What is the minimum qualifying marks and speed required in the AHC RO/ARO typing test?
items.answer: A minimum speed of 25 WPM in English and a minimum score of 17 marks out of 50 are mandatory to qualify.

items.question: How is a 'Word' calculated in standard computer typing speed tests?
items.answer: Every 5 keystrokes (including spaces, punctuation, and characters) are counted as one single word.

items.question: Which CPU register holds the address of the active memory location being read or written?
items.answer: The Memory Address Register (MAR) holds the physical address of the current memory location.

items.question: What is the difference between SMTP and POP3/IMAP protocols?
items.answer: SMTP is a push protocol used to send emails, whereas POP3 and IMAP are pull protocols used to retrieve emails.

traps.title: Common Exam Traps to Avoid
items: The Backspace Trap: Candidates often overuse the backspace key to correct errors, which drastically reduces net speed. In some exam interfaces, backspace is disabled or restricted to the active word. Practice typing without relying heavily on backspace.

Confusing Program Counter (PC) with Instruction Register (IR): The Program Counter (PC) holds the address of the NEXT instruction, while the Instruction Register (IR) holds the CURRENT instruction being executed. Exams often swap these definitions to confuse candidates.

Case Sensitivity and Punctuation Neglect: Missing a capital letter or a comma is evaluated as a Half Mistake (0.05 marks deduction). Accumulating multiple minor formatting errors can drop your score below the mandatory 17-mark qualifying threshold, even if your speed is above 40 WPM.

deepDive.title: Reproducing Exactly A 500 Word English Text Core Study Notes
deepDive.description: Part-B of the Allahabad High Court RO/ARO examination features a mandatory Computer Knowledge and Typing Test. Candidates must reproduce a given 500-word English text on a computer within 20 minutes, requiring a minimum speed of 25 WPM with high accuracy, where evaluation strictly penalizes formatting and spelling errors.

sections.title: Typing Test Parameters & Error Evaluation
sections.content:
Understanding the exact scoring mechanism, speed calculation, and error classification is critical to scoring the minimum qualifying 17 marks out of 50.

  • Minimum Speed Requirement: Candidates must achieve a minimum typing speed of 25 Words Per Minute (WPM) in English on the computer to avoid automatic disqualification.
  • Word Definition in Typing: A standard 'word' is defined as 5 keystrokes (including spaces and punctuation marks). Formula: Gross WPM = (Total Keystrokes / 5) / Time (Minutes).
  • Net Speed Calculation: Net WPM = Gross WPM - (Errors / Time). Only Net WPM and accuracy percentage determine the final merit score out of 50 marks.
  • Formatting Fidelity: The reproduced text must exactly match the source text's indentations, paragraph breaks, bold/italic stylings, and capitalizations.

sections.title: Computer Architecture & CPU Registers
sections.content:
Theoretical computer knowledge is tested alongside practical skills. Understanding CPU operations and memory hierarchy is fundamental.

  • Program Counter (PC): A CPU register that holds the memory address of the next instruction to be fetched and executed. It increments automatically after fetching.
  • Accumulator (AC): A primary register in the ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) used to store intermediate arithmetic and logical results during computation.
  • Memory Address Register (MAR): Holds the memory location of data that needs to be accessed (read from or written to) by the CPU.
  • Instruction Register (IR): Stores the instruction currently being decoded and executed by the control unit of the CPU.

sections.title: MS Word Formatting & Keyboard Shortcuts
sections.content:
Exact text reproduction requires rapid formatting. Mastery of MS Word shortcuts prevents time loss during the exam.

  • Paragraph Alignment: Ctrl + L (Left), Ctrl + R (Right), Ctrl + E (Center), and Ctrl + J (Justify). Justify alignment is highly common in official court judgments.
  • Line Spacing Shortcuts: Ctrl + 1 for Single Spacing, Ctrl + 2 for Double Spacing, and Ctrl + 5 for 1.5 Line Spacing.
  • Font Formatting: Ctrl + B (Bold), Ctrl + I (Italic), Ctrl + U (Underline). Use Ctrl + Shift + D for double underline and Ctrl + Shift + W to underline words only.
  • Non-Breaking Space: Ctrl + Shift + Spacebar creates a space that prevents an automatic line break at that specific position, keeping words together.

sections.title: Internet Protocols & Email Architecture
sections.content:
Networking and email transmission concepts are frequently tested in the theoretical section of the AHC RO/ARO computer paper.

  • SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol): Used for sending emails from a client to a server or between servers. It operates on TCP Port 25 (non-encrypted) or Port 587 (encrypted/TLS).
  • POP3 (Post Office Protocol v3): Downloads emails from the server to a single local device and deletes them from the server by default. Operates on Port 110.
  • IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol): Allows synchronization of emails across multiple devices; emails remain stored on the server. Operates on Port 143.
  • OSI Model Layers: A 7-layer conceptual framework: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, and Application. Routers operate at Layer 3 (Network).
